faqs.q: How long does SEO take to work in Belgium?
faqs.a: Most businesses see early movement in 2 to 3 months and meaningful results in 4 to 6 months. Multilingual setups take slightly longer to build properly, but they are much harder for competitors to copy once they are in place.

faqs.q: Do I need separate websites for Dutch and French?
faqs.a: Usually not. One well-structured site with proper language targeting beats two thin sites. The key is clean separation: Dutch pages for Flanders, French pages for Wallonia, and hreflang done correctly so Google serves the right version.

faqs.q: How much should a business in Belgium budget for SEO?
faqs.a: Multilingual SEO costs more than single-language work because you are effectively building for two or three markets. My pricing is public, and the free audit shows exactly what your situation needs before you spend anything.

faqs.q: Is local SEO different from regular SEO in Belgium?
faqs.a: Yes, and more so than in most countries. Local SEO here means winning the map pack in the right language for each region. A French page will not win Dutch searches in Ghent, no matter how good it is.

faqs.q: Can I do SEO for my Belgian business myself?
faqs.a: You can manage the basics in one language, but the multilingual structure is where most DIY efforts break. Wrong hreflang, mixed-language pages, and duplicate content across languages are the classic self-inflicted wounds I get called in to fix.
